'''Jason S. Campbell''' (born December 31, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]] and was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the first round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. Campbell also played for the [[Oakland Raiders]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. After his playing career, he became an analyst for Auburn Sports Network.{{Citation needed|date=February 2023}}

'''Jason Christopher McAddley''' (born July 28, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played his high school football at [[Oak Ridge High School (Oak Ridge, Tennessee)|Oak Ridge High School]] in [[Oak Ridge, Tennessee]], and played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Richardson | first=Darrell | title=2018 OR Sports Hall of Fame inductees honored on Oct. 19th | website=Oakridger | date=2018-10-17 | url=https://www.oakridger.com/story/sports/2018/10/17/2018-sports-hall-fame-inductees/9527798007/ | access-date=2025-08-26}}</ref>

He was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in [[2004 NFL season|2004]]. He then signed with 49ers in [[2005 NFL season|2005]]. He was signed by the Redskins before the [[2007 NFL season|2007 season]].

'''Jason McEndoo''' (born February 25, 1975) is an American [[American football|football]] coach and former [[Center (American football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[1998 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]]. He is currently a football analyst for [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State University]] in [[Pullman, Washington|Pullman]] and was a member of the [[1997 Washington State Cougars football team|1997]] team which went to the [[1998 Rose Bowl|Rose Bowl]].

Born in [[San Diego]], [[California]], McEndoo played [[high school football]] in southwest [[Washington (state)|Washington]] at  [[Aberdeen High School (Washington)|Aberdeen]]. Selected in the seventh round of the [[1998 NFL draft]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Carpenter |first1=Les |title=Notebook - McEndoo gives Hawks options |work=Seattle Times |date=April 20, 1998 |page=C8}}</ref> McEndoo played one game for Seattle in his rookie season in [[1998 Seattle Seahawks season|1998]]; he was released the following summer on September 5, [[1999 Seattle Seahawks season|1999]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Carpenter |first=Les |title='House' calls it a career; Jackson only surprise cut |work=Seattle Times |date=September 6, 1999 |page=D1}}</ref><ref name=lmtslcut>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=FaxeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=vy4MAAAAIBAJ&pg=2504%2C1449677 |work=Lewiston Morning Tribune |agency=Associated Press |title=Safety Lewis among stars who are cut |date=September 6, 1998 |page=1B}}</ref>

Married for less than a month in [[1996 Washington State Cougars football team|1996]], McEndoo and his wife Michelle were passengers in a rollover accident in which she was killed. The vehicle was driven by teammate Ryan McShane, who apparently fell asleep. The three were returning to Pullman after attending a teammate's wedding in [[Tacoma, Washington|Tacoma]], and occurred on [[Interstate 90 in Washington|Interstate 90]], near [[Ellensburg, Washington|Ellensburg]].<ref name=lmtlaw>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=Ms9eAAAAIBAJ&sjid=8DIMAAAAIBAJ&pg=5969%2C814983 |work=Lewiston Morning Tribune |agency=Associated Press |title=WSU's McEndoo files lawsuit against McShane |date=June 17, 1997 |page=1B}}</ref><ref name=sivlwb>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1997/10/06/232779/the-long-way-back-one-washington-state-player-lost-his-bride-in-a-car-crash-another-his-best-buddy-and-linemate-was-behind-the-wheel-now-the-two-survivors-are-struggling-to-save-their-friendship<!--https://www.si.com/vault/issue/715211/toc-->|magazine=Sports Illustrated |last=Walters |first=John |title=The long way back |date=October 6, 1997 |page=50}}</ref>
